title: SkyTek Scope of Work
description: Every field the SOW template uses. Each x-question is what to ask when the RFP does not answer it.

sow_date.description: Date on the cover, YYYY-MM-DD. Also used in the file name.
sow_date.x-question: What date should the SOW carry? (default: today)

author.description: Who wrote the SOW, shown on the cover. Empty omits the line.
author.x-question: Who should be named as the SOW's author?

client_logo_path.description: Local path to the client's logo (PNG or JPG; SVG cannot be embedded). Empty leaves a labelled placeholder on the cover.
client_logo_path.x-question: Do you have the client's logo as a PNG or JPG to place on the cover? If so, its file path.

client_name.x-question: What is the client's legal name?

client_signatory_name.description: Who signs for the client. Blank leaves a line to fill by hand.
client_signatory_name.x-question: Who signs for the client, if known?

client_signatory_title.description: Job title of the client signatory.
client_signatory_title.x-question: What is the client signatory's title?

project_title.description: Short project name on the cover and footer.

vendor_name.x-question: What is the vendor's legal name?

vendor_signatory_title.description: Job title of the vendor signatory.
vendor_signatory_title.x-question: What is the vendor signatory's title?

msa_reference.description: The master agreement this SOW sits under, e.g. 'Master Services Agreement dated 1 March 2026'. Empty says the SOW stands alone.
msa_reference.x-question: Is there a master services agreement (MSA) this SOW falls under? If so, its name and date.

governing_law.description: Jurisdiction, e.g. 'the Republic of Indonesia'. Empty omits the sentence.
governing_law.x-question: Which jurisdiction's law governs this SOW, if stated?

executive_summary.description: Business value of the engagement and a high-level view of the technical outcome. Line breaks are kept.
executive_summary.x-question: In a few sentences, what problem does the client need solved, and what will this engagement deliver?

objectives.description: Outcomes the work must achieve, one per bullet.
objectives.x-question: What outcomes must this work achieve?

vendor_overview.description: Three or four lines on the vendor's strengths, expertise and track record.
vendor_overview.x-question: How should SkyTek be described in three or four lines (strengths, expertise, track record)?

client_overview.description: The client, its industry, and its current technology relevant to this work.
client_overview.x-question: Briefly, who is the client, what industry are they in, and what do they run today that this work touches?

functional_requirements.description: What the solution does: features and behaviours, one per row.
functional_requirements.x-question: What must the solution do (features, user actions, behaviours)?

non_functional_requirements.description: How well it does it: performance, security, availability, scale. Empty prints a fallback line.
non_functional_requirements.x-question: Any non-functional requirements (performance, security, availability, scale)?

architecture_overview.description: Text overview of the target architecture. Empty prints a line deferring it to the technical design document.
architecture_overview.x-question: Can you describe the target architecture at a high level?

architecture_components.description: Core solution components and each one's role.
architecture_components.x-question: What are the main components of the solution, and what does each do?

integrations.description: In-scope integrations with the client's systems: source, target and purpose.
integrations.x-question: Which of the client's existing systems does the solution integrate with?

focus.description: One or two sentences on what the phase achieves.

tasks.description: Action-verb tasks: design, configure, migrate, test.

phases.description: The work, as phases or workstreams, each with its key tasks.
phases.x-question: How is the work split into phases (e.g. Discovery, Design, Build, UAT, Go-live), and what are the key tasks in each?

description.description: Measurable: state counts, components or environments.

format.description: e.g. Document, Presentation, Code in repository, Demonstration.

deliverables.description: What is handed over, by phase, in which format.
deliverables.x-question: What will be delivered in each phase, and in what format?

acceptance_criteria.description: How the client accepts deliverables. Line breaks are kept.
acceptance_criteria.x-question: How will the client accept deliverables (review window, sign-off)?

out_of_scope.description: Work explicitly excluded. Empty prints 'No exclusions specified.'

default: The Client provides access to the systems, environments and data the work needs before the relevant phase starts.
The Client names a single point of contact and a project sponsor who serves as the escalation point.
The Client makes subject-matter experts available for requirements, design and testing discussions.
The Client makes project decisions within two (2) business days of a request.
The Client is responsible for all cloud, licence and third-party usage fees.
Delays on the Client's side may affect the timeline, the fees or both, and are handled through change control.
assumptions.description: Conditions the estimate depends on. Omitted uses the standard list; an empty list prints 'No assumptions specified.'
assumptions.x-question: Use the standard assumptions (access, point of contact, SMEs, two-day decisions, client pays usage fees, delays go through change control), or add or change some?

risks.description: Shared project risks and how each is mitigated. Empty prints a fallback line.
risks.x-question: What are the main project risks, and how will each be mitigated?

change_control.default: Either party may request a change to this SOW in writing. The Vendor will assess the impact on scope, timeline and fees within five business days. No change takes effect until both parties sign a change order.
change_control.description: How scope changes are handled. Line breaks are kept.
change_control.x-question: Use the standard change-control clause, or a custom one?

success_criteria.description: What a successful project looks like, aligned with the deliverables. 'Completion of all deliverables' is printed first automatically.
success_criteria.x-question: Beyond delivering everything listed, what measurable outcomes mark this project as a success?

start_date.description: Estimated start, YYYY-MM-DD or free text.

end_date.description: Estimated end, YYYY-MM-DD or free text.

activities.description: Key outcomes or deliverables in that period.

timeline.x-question: Roughly which weeks does each phase cover, and what is done in each?

vendor_roles.description: Vendor team roles. Include project management. Mandays and rates belong in effort, not here.
vendor_roles.x-question: Which roles will SkyTek staff (e.g. Engagement Manager, Solution Architect, Engineers), and what does each do?

client_roles.description: Roles the client must provide. Empty prints a fallback line.
client_roles.x-question: Which roles must the client provide (sponsor, product owner, SMEs), and what does each do?

project_type.description: package: a packaged solution priced by item, with no mandays. professional_services: priced by effort, role x mandays x day rate.
project_type.x-question: Is this a packaged solution (priced by item) or professional services (priced by mandays)?

package_items.description: Package projects only: priced lines such as licences, subscriptions or a fixed setup fee. Amounts are computed.
package_items.x-question: What does the package include, in what quantity, at what unit price?

effort.description: Professional-services projects only: mandays and day rate per role. Amounts, total mandays and total cost are computed.
effort.x-question: How many mandays does each role need, and at what day rate?

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD or IDR.

pricing_model.x-question: Is this fixed price, time and materials, or a retainer?

amount.description: Negative for a discount or vendor investment.

fees.description: Extra lines on top of the package items or effort: discounts (negative), third-party costs, one-off fees. The total must not be negative.
fees.x-question: Any other fees or discounts on top of that?

deliverables.description: Deliverables that must be accepted before this payment.

due.description: Estimated completion: date or free text.

payment_schedule.description: When each payment is invoiced, and what it depends on.
payment_schedule.x-question: When is each payment invoiced, for how much, and which deliverables does it depend on?

payment_terms.x-question: What are the payment terms (e.g. Net 30)?

expenses.default: Expenses, where agreed in advance between the Client and the Vendor, are paid by the Client in line with the Client's expense reimbursement policy. Expenses invoiced by the Vendor that the Client does not object to in writing are payable.
expenses.description: Expense clause. Line breaks are kept.
expenses.x-question: Use the standard expenses clause (pre-agreed expenses reimbursed by the client), or a custom one?

tax_treatment.description: Whether the fees include sales tax or VAT.
tax_treatment.x-question: Are the fees exclusive or inclusive of sales tax / VAT?

_sources.description: Where each field's value came from. Not rendered.
